          Real-life example 5
          Placing the checklist on the Lab 3 calendar with constraint checks
          
 
          TaskPlace every item of the Lesson 3 checklist on a Lab 3 course day, check business hours and the change freeze, and produce a calendar file with the kick-off, three test sessions and the closing meeting.
          Relation to the lectureApplies the contents of a plan (5.2), the constraints and dependencies (5.4) and the two meetings (5.5).
          Future labsLab 2 Part B step 6 (schedule) and step 7 (meetings); Lab 3 on Days 7-10; Project section 5.
          
 
          The script reads Lab2B_audit_checklist.csv, written by the Lesson 3 example. Items tested with the baseline tools of Part A (MC-01, MC-02, MC-08) go to Day 7; configuration items checked with scripts (MC-03 to MC-07) go to Day 8; control items go to Day 9. The segmentation scan MC-19 is flagged as a test that may affect availability; the script checks that its session starts after 18:00 (Day 9, 19:45) and that no session is on or after November 20.
          

          The script then converts Eastern times to UTC (Coordinated Universal Time) and writes an iCalendar file with five events: the kick-off on November 11 at 19:45, the three test sessions and the closing meeting on November 18 at 21:30. Import the file into any calendar application to see the schedule. The same schedule appears in sheet B5 of the Lab 2 template.
          
 

          
 
          L5_schedule_plan.sh - Bash (Linux, WSL)
  
  
  
  
  
  
 
          
 
          
  
          Code - a comment line explains every code line74 lines
          1#!/usr/bin/env bash
          2# TASK: place every checklist item of the plan on a Lab 3 course day, check two constraints
          3#       (scans outside business hours, nothing inside the Black Friday change freeze) and
          4#       produce a schedule file plus an iCalendar (.ics) file with the kick-off meeting, the
          5#       test sessions and the closing meeting.
          6# RELATION TO THE LECTURE: Lesson 5 - scheduling and planning compliance assessment
          7#       activities (dates, constraints, meetings, communication).
          8# FUTURE LABS: Lab 2 Part B step 6 (schedule) and step 7 (meetings); Lab 3 (Days 7-10).
          9#       Input: Lab2B_audit_checklist.csv written by the Lesson 3 example.
          10 
          11# Stop at the first error, treat unset variables as errors and detect failures inside pipes.
          12set -euo pipefail
          13# Input checklist (semicolon-separated) produced by the Lesson 3 example.
          14CHECKLIST="Lab2B_audit_checklist.csv"
          15# Output files: the schedule table and the calendar file.
          16SCHEDULE="Lab2B_schedule.csv"; ICS="Lab2B_assessment.ics"
          17# Date of each Lab 3 course day (associative array: key = day name).
          18declare -A DAY_DATE=([Day7]="2026-11-11" [Day8]="2026-11-14" [Day9]="2026-11-17" [Day10]="2026-11-18")
          19# Start of the lab block of each day (after the lecture and the break), Eastern time.
          20declare -A LAB_START=([Day7]="19:45" [Day8]="09:45" [Day9]="19:45" [Day10]="19:45")
          21# End of the lab block of each day.
          22declare -A LAB_END=([Day7]="22:00" [Day8]="13:30" [Day9]="22:00" [Day10]="22:00")
          23# First day of the change freeze: no test may take place on or after this date.
          24FREEZE_START="2026-11-20"
          25 
          26# Write the header line of the schedule file.
          27echo "id;title;day;date;start;constraint_check" > "$SCHEDULE"
          28# Read the checklist line by line (tail -n +2 skips the header line).
          29while IFS=';' read -r id title type cis iso pci csf assets lab3; do
          30  # Choose the course day from the Lab 3 part recorded in the checklist.
          31  case "$lab3" in
          32    # Baseline tools (Part A, or Parts A-B for cloud demo evidence) run on Day 7.
          33    *"Part A"*|*"Parts A-B"*) day="Day7" ;;
          34    # Check scripts and patch status (Part B) run on Day 8.
          35    *"Part B"*) day="Day8" ;;
          36    # Controls, segmentation and access (Part C) are verified on Day 9.
          37    *) day="Day9" ;;
          38  esac
          39  # Default result of the constraint checks.
          40  check="ok"
          41  # Network scans (MC-19 uses Nmap) must start after 18:00, outside business hours.
          42  if [[ "$id" == "MC-19" ]]; then
          43    # Compare the start time as text (HH:MM sorts correctly); move the scan if it is too early.
          44    if [[ "${LAB_START[$day]}" < "18:00" ]]; then day="Day9"; check="moved: scan outside business hours"; else check="ok: scan after 18:00"; fi
          45  fi
          46  # Refuse any date inside the change freeze (YYYY-MM-DD strings compare like dates).
          47  if [[ ! "${DAY_DATE[$day]}" < "$FREEZE_START" ]]; then check="CONFLICT: change freeze"; fi
          48  # Append the scheduled line to the schedule file.
          49  echo "$id;$title;$day;${DAY_DATE[$day]};${LAB_START[$day]};$check" >> "$SCHEDULE"
          50  # Print one confirmation line per item.
          51  echo "$id -> $day ${DAY_DATE[$day]} ${LAB_START[$day]} ($check)"
          52done < <(tail -n +2 "$CHECKLIST")
          53 
          54# Convert a Montreal date and time into UTC, the format used inside the calendar file.
          55to_utc() { date -u -d "TZ=\"America/Toronto\" $1 $2" +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ; }
          56# Write the mandatory iCalendar header lines (each line ends with CR LF, as RFC 5545 requires).
          57printf 'BEGIN:VCALENDAR\r\nVERSION:2.0\r\nPRODID:-//Cyber.SoHo//420-D04-AB Lab 2B//EN\r\n' > "$ICS"
          58# Define a helper that appends one event: UID, date, start time, end time, summary.
          59add_event() { printf 'BEGIN:VEVENT\r\nUID:%s@cyber-soho-lab\r\nDTSTAMP:%s\r\nDTSTART:%s\r\nDTEND:%s\r\nSUMMARY:%s\r\nEND:VEVENT\r\n' "$1" "$(to_utc 2026-11-07 08:30)" "$(to_utc "$2" "$3")" "$(to_utc "$2" "$4")" "$5" >> "$ICS"; }
          60# Kick-off (opening) meeting at the start of the Day 7 lab block, before the first test.
          61add_event "kickoff" "${DAY_DATE[Day7]}" "19:45" "20:00" "Kick-off meeting - conformity assessment of Erable Cycles"
          62# Add one test session per day that has scheduled items.
          63for day in Day7 Day8 Day9; do
          64  # Collect the item IDs scheduled on this day from the schedule file.
          65  items=$(awk -F';' -v d="$day" '$3 == d {printf "%s ", $1}' "$SCHEDULE")
          66  # Create the event only when the day has at least one item.
          67  if [[ -n "$items" ]]; then add_event "tests-$day" "${DAY_DATE[$day]}" "${LAB_START[$day]}" "${LAB_END[$day]}" "Tests: ${items% }"; fi
          68done
          69# Closing meeting at the end of Day 10, after the last verification.
          70add_event "closing" "${DAY_DATE[Day10]}" "21:30" "21:50" "Closing meeting - preliminary findings"
          71# Close the calendar.
          72printf 'END:VCALENDAR\r\n' >> "$ICS"
          73# Print a summary: number of scheduled items and number of events in the calendar.
          74echo "Scheduled: $(($(wc -l < "$SCHEDULE") - 1)) items; calendar events: $(grep -c 'BEGIN:VEVENT' "$ICS") -> $ICS"
          75

            Run it yourself. Run bash L5_schedule_plan.sh in the folder that contains Lab2B_audit_checklist.csv (Linux, WSL on Windows, or the Ubuntu lab VM (virtual machine); GNU date is required). Import Lab2B_assessment.ics into any calendar application.
            
 
            Step-by-step explanation
            1. set -euo pipefail stops the script at the first error, so a missing file cannot produce a wrong calendar.
            2. The associative array LAB_START stores the start time of the lab block of each course day.
            3. The while loop reads the checklist line by line with IFS=';' and skips the header line.
            4. A case statement assigns Part A items to Day 7, Part B items to Day 8 and the other items to Day 9.
            5. For MC-19 the script compares the start time with 18:00, and for every item it compares the date with the freeze date.
            6. The function to_utc() uses date with TZ=America/Toronto to convert Eastern times to UTC (EST (Eastern Standard Time) is UTC-5 after November 1).
            7. The calendar file is written with CRLF line endings, as the iCalendar format requires, and the summary line is printed.

            6
            Lesson 6 - From plan to evidence: the Lab 2 Part B deliverable
            About 10 minutes - course plan topic: Synthesis - the assessment plan, Lab 2 summary and Mid-Term preparation
            
 
            
 
            6.1 The six sections of the plan and their sources 
            

            The Lab 2 Part B plan joins the results of the five previous lessons. Section 1 (scope) uses the five critical assets and the two VMs (virtual machines) from Part A. Section 2 (mandate) is the authorization letter. Section 3 (checklist) is the result of the Lesson 3 rules. Section 4 (tests) applies Lessons 1 and 2. Section 5 (risk method) is the matrix of Lesson 4. Section 6 (schedule and meetings) is the result of Lesson 5. The plan is written with Lab2B_Plan_Template_420-D04-AB.docx; its tables match the sheets B1 to B5 of the Lab 2 template workbook, so one source of information feeds both files.
            6.2 From plan to evidence: what happens in Lab 3 
            

            In Lab 3, every checklist item becomes a test record: the auditor executes the procedure written in section 4, saves the evidence with the naming rule, computes its SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm, 256-bit) fingerprint, adds a line to the evidence index and records the result. Every nonconformity becomes a finding (condition, criterion, cause, effect) rated with the section 5 matrix. A plan that defines a measurable pass rule and an evidence file name for every item makes Lab 3 a matter of execution; a plan that says "check the firewall" forces you to redesign the test during the lab.
            6.3 Readiness check and common mistakes 
            

            The Part B rubric gives 5 points: scope and mandate (1), checklist quality and mapping (2), test methods and evidence (1), risk scales and schedule (1). The Lesson 6 example checks a draft plan against this rubric before submission.
            

            Common mistakeWhy it loses pointsCorrection
            

            Mandate not signed or not datedNo authorization means no test (Legal Notice 6.1)Sign and date it before November 11
            

            Checklist items without framework referencesThe crosswalk is part of the checklist gradeFill the CIS (Center for Internet Security), ISO (International Organization for Standardization), PCI and CSF (Cybersecurity Framework) columns, or "-" with a reason
            

            Pass rule not measurable ("firewall OK")The test cannot give an objective verdictWrite a value or a condition that can be true or false
            

            Sample without size or reasonThe selection cannot be verified"10 of 45: J1, J2 + 5 random, seed 20261107"
            

            Scan planned during business hours or after Nov 20Violates the case constraintsDay 9 after 18:00
            

            Asset IDs different between Part A and Part BBreaks traceabilityReuse the Part A IDs everywhere
            

            Copied ISO text or real personal informationLicensing and privacy rules (Legal Notice 7.5, 6.7)Cite control numbers; mask personal information
            6.4 Lab 2 in summary 
            

            This lecture prepares Lab 2; the full step-by-step instructions are in the Lab 2 guide. Part A (5 points): complete the inventory of the 12 assets with the 12 columns, collect evidence from your two VMs (virtual machines), classify every asset with the decision table and justify the five critical assets. Part B (5 points): write the six-section assessment plan described in this lecture, including the signed authorization letter. You submit two files - LastName_FirstName_420-D04-AB_Lab2.xlsx and LastName_FirstName_420-D04-AB_Lab2.pdf - in the DropBox of the course in Omnivox LÉA by Sunday, November 15, 2026, 23:59 Eastern time (EST (Eastern Standard Time), UTC-5, since daylight saving time ended on November 1). Lab 2 is worth 10 % of the final grade.
            6.5 Preparing the Mid-Term (Day 6, Tuesday, November 10, 18:30) 
            

            The Mid-Term examination contains 25 multiple-choice questions (one answer) and 15 multiple-select questions (the number of expected answers is shown in round brackets), in 90 minutes, for 20 % of the final grade. The distribution of the 40 questions is: introduction to conformity assessment 8, laws and regulations 12, frameworks and documentation 8, asset inventory and classification 6, assessment methodologies (today) 6. The average time is 2.25 minutes per question. Review method: the flashcards and the questions of each lesson, then the Day 5 practice tests in quiz mode with the timer of your phone.
            Key terms to learn - Lesson 6
            Evidence index
            A table with one line per evidence file: name, item, date, SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm, 256-bit), description.
            Test record
            The completed test card: procedure executed, actual result, verdict, evidence reference.
            Readiness check
            A self-assessment of a draft against the rubric before submission.
            Traceability
            The ability to follow an item from the requirement to the asset, the test, the evidence and the finding.

            • What would you write in section 4 for MC-09 (host firewall) so that the test is measurable?

            Real-life example 6
            Readiness check of a draft assessment plan
            
 
            TaskAssemble the six sections of the Part B plan from the files produced by the previous examples, score the draft against the Part B rubric and list the fixes before submission.
            Relation to the lectureJoins the results of Lessons 1-5 into the six sections (6.1) and applies the rubric and the list of common mistakes (6.3).
            Future labsLab 2 Part B deliverable (due Sunday, November 15, 23:59 EST (Eastern Standard Time)), Project sections 2 and 5, Course Procedure Manual chapters 2 and 3.
            
 
            The script reads the mandate (L6_mandate.json), the checklist written in Lesson 3, the test methods table, the risk scales of Lesson 4 and the schedule of Lesson 5. It checks every criterion of the Part B rubric: the scope and the mandate fields, the number of items and their mapping, the completeness of method, sample, pass rule and evidence, the risk scales and the schedule.
            

            The draft obtains 4.5 of 5: the mandate has no signature date, so "Scope and mandate" receives 0.5 instead of 1. The script prints the fix - "fill in signed_on; sign and date it before 2026-11-11" - and writes the draft plan in Markdown (Lab2B_Assessment_Plan_DRAFT.md), which you can compare with your own document.
            
 

            
 
            L6_plan_assembler.py - Python 3
  
  
  
  
  
  
 
            
 
            
  
            Code - a comment line explains every code line105 lines
            1# TASK: assemble the six sections of the Lab 2 Part B Assessment Plan from the files
            2#       produced by the earlier examples, check the plan against the 5-point rubric and
            3#       list the fixes still needed before submission.
            4# RELATION TO THE LECTURE: Lesson 6 - from plan to evidence. The plan joins scope, mandate,
            5#       checklist (Lesson 3), test methods (Lesson 2), risk scales (Lesson 4) and schedule
            6#       (Lesson 5) into one document that management can approve.
            7# FUTURE LABS: Lab 2 Part B deliverable, Project sections 2 and 5, Course Procedure Manual
            8#       chapter 3. Inputs are fictional course files; no real personal information.
            9 
            10# Import csv to read the semicolon-separated tables and json to read the structured files.
            11import csv, json
            12 
            13# The seven in-scope assets decided in Lab 2 Part A (5 critical assets and 2 lab VMs).
            14SCOPE = ["A01", "A03", "A04", "A07", "A10", "V01", "V02"]
            15# Date of the first test (Day 7): the mandate must be signed before this date.
            16FIRST_TEST = "2026-11-11"
            17 
            18# Define a helper that reads a semicolon-separated file into a list of dictionaries.
            19def read_table(name):
            20    # Open the file with UTF-8 encoding and let DictReader use the first line as header.
            21    with open(name, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            22        # Return every row as a dictionary.
            23        return list(csv.DictReader(f, delimiter=";"))
            24 
            25# Read the checklist (Lesson 3), the schedule (Lesson 5) and the test methods (Lesson 2).
            26checklist = read_table("Lab2B_audit_checklist.csv")
            27# Index the schedule by item ID so that the day of any item can be found directly.
            28schedule = {r["id"]: r for r in read_table("Lab2B_schedule.csv")}
            29# Index the test methods by item ID as well.
            30tests = {r["id"]: r for r in read_table("L6_test_methods.csv")}
            31# Read the risk scales (Lesson 4) and the mandate fields typed by the student.
            32scales = json.load(open("L4_risk_scales.json", encoding="utf-8"))
            33# The mandate holds the authorization letter fields (owner, systems, period, contact, signature date).
            34mandate = json.load(open("L6_mandate.json", encoding="utf-8"))
            35 
            36# Create the score table of the rubric and the list of fixes.
            37score, fixes = {}, []
            38# Criterion 1 (1 point): every in-scope asset is tested by at least one item ...
            39covered = {a for row in checklist for a in row["assets"].split("|")}
            40# ... which earns the first half point.
            41score["Scope and mandate"] = 0.5 if set(SCOPE) <= covered else 0.0
            42# ... and the mandate is complete and signed before the first test (second half point).
            43missing = [k for k in ("owner", "systems", "period", "contact", "signed_on") if not mandate.get(k)]
            44# Give the half point only when nothing is missing and the signature date precedes the first test.
            45if not missing and mandate["signed_on"] < FIRST_TEST:
            46    # The mandate is valid.
            47    score["Scope and mandate"] += 0.5
            48else:
            49    # Record what must be fixed in the authorization letter.
            50    fixes.append(f"Mandate: fill in {', '.join(missing) or 'signed_on'}; sign and date it before {FIRST_TEST}")
            51 
            52# Criterion 2 (2 points): size, balance, mapping and asset coverage of the checklist.
            53n_config = sum(1 for r in checklist if r["type"] == "C")
            54# Count the control items (technical, administrative, segmentation / access).
            55n_control = sum(1 for r in checklist if r["type"] in ("T", "A", "S"))
            56# A line is "mapped" when it carries at least two framework references.
            57mapped = all(sum(1 for fw in ("cis", "iso", "pci", "csf") if r[fw] and not r[fw].startswith("-")) >= 2 for r in checklist)
            58# Add half a point for each of the four checks.
            59score["Checklist quality and mapping"] = 0.5 * sum([12 <= len(checklist) <= 15, n_config >= 3 and n_control >= 3, mapped, set(SCOPE) <= covered])
            60 
            61# Criterion 3 (1 point): every item states method, sample, expected result and evidence.
            62complete = [r["id"] for r in checklist if all(tests.get(r["id"], {}).get(k) for k in ("method", "sample", "expected", "evidence"))]
            63# The score is proportional to the number of complete items.
            64score["Test methods and evidence"] = round(len(complete) / len(checklist), 2)
            65 
            66# Criterion 4 (1 point): three-level scales for likelihood and impact, and a valid schedule.
            67scales_ok = len(scales["likelihood"]) == 3 and len(scales["impact"]) == 3
            68# The schedule is valid when every item is scheduled and every constraint check starts with "ok".
            69schedule_ok = all(r["id"] in schedule and schedule[r["id"]]["constraint_check"].startswith("ok") for r in checklist)
            70# Add half a point for each of the two checks.
            71score["Risk scales and schedule"] = 0.5 * scales_ok + 0.5 * schedule_ok
            72 
            73# Build the Markdown text of the plan, one section after the other.
            74md = ["# Assessment Plan (DRAFT) - Erable Cycles inc. (fictional case)", ""]
            75# Section 1: scope and objectives.
            76md += ["## 1. Scope and objectives", "In scope: " + ", ".join(SCOPE) + ". Objective: verify conformity with the requirements identified in Lab 1.", ""]
            77# Section 2: mandate and authorization (fields of the letter).
            78md += ["## 2. Mandate and authorization"] + [f"- {k}: {v if v else '(missing)'}" for k, v in mandate.items()] + [""]
            79# Section 3: the audit checklist with its framework references.
            80md += ["## 3. Audit checklist", "| ID | Item | Type | CIS v8.1 | ISO/IEC 27001 | PCI DSS | NIST CSF |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
            81# One table line per checklist item.
            82md += [f"| {r['id']} | {r['title']} | {r['type']} | {r['cis']} | {r['iso']} | {r['pci']} | {r['csf']} |" for r in checklist] + [""]
            83# Section 4: test methods, samples and expected evidence.
            84md += ["## 4. Test methods, samples and expected evidence", "| ID | Method | Sample | Expected result | Evidence |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
            85# One table line per item, taken from the test-method file.
            86md += [f"| {r['id']} | {tests[r['id']]['method']} | {tests[r['id']]['sample']} | {tests[r['id']]['expected']} | {tests[r['id']]['evidence']} |" for r in checklist] + [""]
            87# Section 5: risk method with the one-line definition of every level.
            88md += ["## 5. Risk method (3x3: score = likelihood x impact)"] + [f"- Likelihood {s} {n}: {d}" for s, n, d in scales["likelihood"]] + [f"- Impact {s} {n}: {d}" for s, n, d in scales["impact"]] + ["- Levels: 1-2 Low, 3-4 Medium, 6 High, 9 Critical", ""]
            89# Section 6: schedule, then the two meetings.
            90md += ["## 6. Schedule, tools and communication"] + [f"- {schedule[r['id']]['date']} {schedule[r['id']]['start']} {r['id']} {r['title']}" for r in checklist]
            91# Agendas of the kick-off and closing meetings (three bullets each in the final plan).
            92md += ["- Kick-off 2026-11-11 19:45: objectives and scope, schedule and contacts, evidence and confidentiality rules", "- Closing 2026-11-18 21:30: preliminary findings, rating method, report date", ""]
            93# Save the draft plan to a Markdown file.
            94open("Lab2B_Assessment_Plan_DRAFT.md", "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(md))
            95 
            96# Print the rubric line by line, then the total out of 5.
            97for criterion, points in score.items():
            98    # Each line shows the criterion and the points obtained.
            99    print(f"{criterion}: {points}")
            100# Print the readiness total.
            101print(f"Readiness: {sum(score.values())}/5 - plan written to Lab2B_Assessment_Plan_DRAFT.md")
            102# Print every fix that remains before submission.
            103for fix in fixes:
            104    # One line per fix.
            105    print("Fix before submitting:", fix)
            106

              Run it yourself. Put L6_plan_assembler.py in the folder that contains the outputs of the previous examples and the two input files (L6_mandate.json, L6_test_methods.csv, plus L4_risk_scales.json), then run python3 L6_plan_assembler.py.
              
 
              Step-by-step explanation
              1. csv and json read the tables (semicolon-separated) and the structured files produced by the earlier examples.
              2. The mandate is loaded; the script checks that every field of the Annex D letter is filled, including signed_on.
              3. The checklist is loaded and the script counts the items (14) and the lines that carry the four framework references.
              4. For each item, the test-method table must give a method, a sample, an expected result and an evidence file name.
              5. The risk scales must define three levels for likelihood and impact; the schedule must avoid the freeze and respect business hours.
              6. Each rubric criterion receives its points; the total is the readiness score (4.5 / 5).
              7. The six sections are written to a Markdown draft and the list of fixes is printed.
              
 
              🐍 Script: L6_plan_assembler.py 📄 Input: L6_mandate.json 📄 Input: L6_test_methods.csv 📝 Expected draft plan: Lab2B_Assessment_Plan_DRAFT.md

              Q1MCQ - one correct answer
              

              In the readiness example, why does 'Scope and mandate' receive 0.5 instead of 1?
              1. AThe authorization letter has no signature date (signed_on is empty)
                Correct. An unsigned or undated mandate does not authorize the tests.
              2. BThe scope contains too many assets
                The scope (5 critical assets + 2 VMs (virtual machines)) is complete.
              3. CThe checklist has only 14 items
                14 is within the required 12-15.
              4. DThe risk scales are missing
                The risk scales receive their full point.
              

              

              Look at the fix printed at the end.
              Q2MCQ - one correct answer
              

              Which test definition for MC-09 (host firewall) is acceptable in section 4 of the plan?
              1. ARe-perform Get-NetFirewallProfile on LAB-WIN11 and sudo ufw status verbose on LAB-UBUNTU; pass: all profiles on, inbound default deny; evidence L3-E12_MC-09_firewall.txt
                Correct. Every part of the test is defined and the pass rule is measurable.
              2. BCheck the firewall
                No method detail, sample, pass rule or evidence.
              3. CFirewall OK
                This is a result, not a test definition, and it is not measurable.
              4. DAsk the administrator whether the firewall is on
                An interview alone, with no pass rule or evidence file.
              

              

              Method, sample, measurable pass rule and evidence name.
